cards.text: That same day, right after the question about Caesar's coin (Matthew 22:15-22), the Sadducees come to Jesus with a question of their own. It's like clearing out your inbox and hearing that DING before you even sit back down. The Sadducees are a party tied to the high priest (Acts 5:17), and Matthew tells us one big thing about what they believe.

cards.question: Matthew says the Sadducees who come to Jesus believe the dead will rise again.

cards.text: They call Him Teacher, and then they bring up a rule from Moses. If a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow.

cards.question: In the rule from Moses the Sadducees quote, why does the brother marry the widow?

answers.text: To raise up children for his brother
To pay off his brother's debts
To look after his brother's flocks

cards.text: Then they tell Jesus about seven brothers among them. The first one marries and dies without having children, so he leaves his wife to his brother.

cards.question: In the Sadducees' story, the second brother has a child with the widow, and that's where it stops.

cards.text: And last of all, the woman dies. Now the Sadducees lean in for the big finish.

cards.question: Now the Sadducees ask Jesus their big question about the resurrection. What do they want to know about the woman?

answers.text: Which brother will be her husband
Which brother she loved the most
Which brother will inherit her land

cards.text: Jesus doesn't tiptoe around it. He tells them flat out they're mistaken.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Sadducees they're mistaken. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They don't know the Scriptures or God's power
They spoke without asking the priests first
They brought their question on the Sabbath

cards.question: Jesus tells the Sadducees that in the resurrection, people will keep marrying just like they do now.
Jesus says that in the resurrection, people will be like the ___ in heaven.

cards.text: Then Jesus takes on the bigger question, whether the dead rise at all. He asks the Sadducees if they've never read what God said to them.
Jesus quotes God's own words: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob". Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are Israel's forefathers (Acts 3:13).

cards.question: Jesus says God is not the God of the ___, but of the ___.
When the crowds hear Jesus answer the Sadducees, how do they react?

answers.text: They are astonished at His teaching
They turn and walk away quietly
They ask Jesus to explain it again

cards.text: Question after question, and Jesus is still standing. Stick around, friend, because this day's not done yet.

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time only as the source of a rule. The card never says simply who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out "angels" rather than "stars" or "elders." The blank asks for wording from a line the baker has not yet seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
